topic: Area of Study 1: Western Classical Tradition 1650-1910
subject: music

items.title: When Vivaldi was rediscovered
items.claim: After Vivaldi's death in 1741 his music largely disappeared from concert programmes. When did serious revival begin?

options.text: Within ten years of his death
The 1920s-1950s, after manuscript discoveries in Turin

items.reveal:
Manuscripts found in monastic libraries reached the Biblioteca Nazionale di Torino in the 1920s-1930s. Recording, especially after 1950, restored Vivaldi to the canon.

The Four Seasons (1725) is now among the most recorded works in classical music.
items.why: Canonical status is reconstructed, not fixed; archival luck matters.

items.title: When Schoenberg formalised twelve-tone technique
items.claim: Arnold Schoenberg's 'method of composing with twelve tones related only to one another' was first described publicly in approximately which year?
items.reveal_title: The technique was described in the early 1920s
items.reveal:
Schoenberg discussed the technique with students around 1921-1923; his Suite for Piano Op. 25 (1923) is one of the first fully serial works.

Webern, Berg and later Boulez and Stockhausen extended the method.
items.why: Major shifts in musical language can be tracked to specific compositional methods.
